headline: Approved resolutions, budget authorizations, and a bond resolution for city improvement projects.
summary: The committee approved four resolutions amending community improvement programs for projects including a hazardous materials grant, oral health program, Canal St Multi-Modal Trail, and opioid litigation settlement trust. It also approved budget authorizations tied to those resolutions and voted to advance a $27,000 bond resolution for a Women's Locker Room Expansion, which will lay over for further action.
decisions: Approved four resolutions amending community improvement programs, including funding for a hazardous materials grant, oral health program, Canal St trail, and a decrease to the opioid litigation settlement trust.
Approved budget authorizations for listed projects, subject to final adoption of related resolutions.
Passed the bond resolution for $27,000 for the Women's Locker Room Expansion, to lay over.

COMMITTEE ON FINANCE 
August 4, 2026 Upon Recess of the BMA 
 
Mayor Ruais called the meeting to order.  
 
The Clerk called the roll. 
 
Present: Aldermen Kaw-uh, Goonan, Dexter, Fajardo, Bonilla, Kantor, Trisciani, 
  O’Neil, Terrio, Sapienza, Burkush, Barry, Vincent, Thomas 
 
1. Resolutions:  
 
“Amending the FY2027 Community Improvement Program, authorizing and 
appropriating funds in the amount of Thirty-Three Thousand Dollars ($33,000) for 
the FY2027 CIPC300040327 Hazardous Materials Grant.” 
 
“Amending the FY2026 Community Improvement Program, authorizing and 
appropriating funds in the amount of Twenty-Three Thousand Six Hundred Five 
Dollars and Ninety-Nine Cents ($23,605.99) for the FY2026 CIP C410021726 
Oral Health Program.” 
 
“Amending the FY2022 and FY2027 Community Improvement Program, 
authorizing, appropriating and transferring funds in the amount of One Million 
One Hundred Thousand Dollars($1,100,000) for the FY2027 CIP C500070427 
Canal St Multi-Modal Trail (TAP 4).” 
 
“Amending the FY2023 Community Improvement Program, decreasing funds in 
the amount of Seventy Thousand Dollars ($70,000) for the FY2023 211723 
Opioid Litigation Settlement Trust.” 
 
On motion of Alderman O’Neil, duly seconded by Alderman Sapienza, it was voted to 
waive the reading by titles only. 
 
On motion of Alderman Terrio, duly seconded by Alderman Sapienza, it was voted 
that the Resolutions ought to pass and be Enrolled.
August 4, 2026 COMMITTEE ON FINANCE 
Page 2 of 3 
 
2. Budget Authorizations: 
• 711422 Trail Construction 
• 810625 MUNIS ERP Financial System 
• 811025 Independent City Auditor 
• C200060326 Dilapidated Building Demolition 
• C270070327 MS4 FY27 Permit Compliance 
• C300040327 Hazardous Materials Grant 
• C410021726 Oral Health Program 
• C500070427 Canal St Multi-Modal Trail (TAP 4) 
• 211723 Opioid Litigation Settlement Trust 
 
On motion of Alderman O’Neil, duly seconded by Alderman Burkush, it was that the 
Budget Authorizations be approved subject to final adoption of related Resolutions. 
 
Matthew Normand, City Clerk: As we mentioned earlier, five minutes ago, that bond has 
been referred to the committee. That's a vote that needs to be taken so that it comes back 
and lays over. 
 
 Bond Resolution: 
 
“Authorizing Bonds, Notes or Lease Purchases in the amount of Twenty Seven 
Thousand Dollars ($27,000) for the 2026 CIP C330040426 Women’s Locker 
Room Expansion." 
 
On motion of Alderman Burkush, duly seconded by Alderman Barry, it was voted to 
read by title only. 
 
On motion of Alderman Burkush, duly seconded by Alderman Barry, it was voted that 
the Bond Resolution ought to pass and layover. 
 
There being no further business, on motion of Alderman Burkush, duly seconded by 
Alderman Sapienza, it was voted to adjourn.
August 4, 2026 COMMITTEE ON FINANCE 
Page 3 of 3 
 
A True Record.  Attest. 
 
     
      City Clerk
